title: Paid "warranty activation" through a link vs. free warranty registration reminder
summary: The recipient bought a Voltrix television on ShopKart last week. A caller from "Voltrix customer care" phones about warranty registration. In the legitimate case, the agent reminds the recipient that registration is free, done by entering the serial number and invoice in the Voltrix app, and mentions that an optional extended warranty can be bought in the app later. In the fraud case, the caller says the standard warranty will be void unless an "activation fee" is paid today through a link sent by SMS. Both callers say "warranty", "registration", and quote the same price; in `_L` the price belongs to an optional extended warranty.

shared_setting.recipient_profile: the buyer; profile sampled at generation.
other_facts: Product: a Voltrix LED television worth [AMOUNT_23] (₹12,000–₹45,000), delivered and installed last week.
Both callers know the model and purchase date.

fraud.label_rationale: The caller claims the free standard warranty will not apply unless a fee is paid through a link sent by SMS. Charging to "activate" a warranty that comes with the product, through an off-platform link, is a payment scam.
fraud.caller_objective: Collect [AMOUNT_22] and card details through the link.
stable_facts: The caller says the warranty "lapses tonight" without activation.
The link arrives from a mobile number as https://voltrix-warranty.invalid/activate.
The caller does not ask for the serial number or invoice.

legitimate.label_rationale: The agent reminds the recipient to register the product for free in the official app. The paid extended warranty is optional, offered for later, and bought only in the app.
legitimate.caller_objective: Get the product registered and mention the optional extended warranty.
stable_facts: Registration is free: serial number (on the back of the TV) plus a photo of the invoice, entered in the Voltrix app.
The standard warranty runs from the invoice date whether or not the recipient registers; registering speeds up service visits (fictional Voltrix rule).
An optional extended warranty costs [AMOUNT_22] and can be bought in the app at any time within the first year.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud caller may reduce the fee, resend the link, or stress the deadline. They must not switch to OTPs, remote access, or card details read out on the call. The legitimate agent must not send any payment link or press the recipient to buy the extended warranty now.

must_preserve: void-unless-paid claim and SMS link in _F
free in-app registration and optional extended warranty in _L

ambiguities: Paid extended warranties are real and can be sold by phone; the price mention is a deliberate confound in _L.
In this family the label rests on the claim that the standard warranty needs a fee and on payment through an SMS link.
The rule that the Voltrix standard warranty runs from the invoice date without registration is a fictional fact of this card.

evidence_references.claim: A major marketplace never asks for payment information over the phone; verify in the account (CE13)
Do not make payments through links in unsolicited messages (CE17)
A standard manufacturer warranty is free and starts from invoice date
